objective: Detect capability-envelope drift between agent/model/tool/route admission and use by comparing bound manifest digests, generations, key epochs, task/audience/route identities, lifecycle state, and revocation evidence without fabricating cryptographic attestation.

research_inputs.finding: SPIFFE provides stable workload identifiers, short-lived X.509/JWT SVIDs, automatically rotated keys, and trust bundles; workload identity and attestation are infrastructure responsibilities.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL binds manifest freshness to agent/task/audience/route and marks cryptographic attestation as not performed; it remains compatible with future SPIFFE-backed enforcement.

research_inputs.finding: Capability-bound agent certificates and a skills-manifest hash address silent capability escalation when tools or models change after authorization; governance also needs verifiable interaction records.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL compares admitted and observed manifest digests, model identity/version, tool set, route, generation, and key epoch, rejecting drift before a use receipt is admitted.

research_inputs.finding: Verifiable delegation across MCP/A2A benefits from self-certifying or resolved identities, signed identity documents, key rotation, capability attenuation, lifecycle expiry, and provenance-bound completion records.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL accepts a delegation-hop digest, enforces bounded expiry and key epochs, and composes with the existing delegation-chain verifier without issuing credentials or implementing transport bindings.

features: same-generation snapshot handling with generation rollback rejection
key epoch and monotonic revocation evidence
use/nonce replay and digest tamper protection

benchmark.scope: local Python control-plane receipt overhead; excludes cryptographic attestation, identity providers, live process inspection, network, tools, models, storage, and kernel scheduling latency

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the capability-freshness module, tests, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain prior tagged delegation-chain release

limitations: This verifier compares caller-supplied manifest snapshots; it does not inspect a live agent process, model binary, tool implementation, route, or workload identity provider.
The evidence does not perform X.509/JWT/Ed25519 verification, TPM/TEE attestation, SPIFFE issuance, key rotation, or revocation distribution.
The benchmark measures local Python receipt overhead and excludes cryptographic, identity-provider, network, storage, model, tool, accelerator, and kernel scheduler performance.

The real-task validation is a deterministic local fixture and does not establish production capability integrity, multi-host interoperability, agent quality, general intelligence, browser autonomy, or robotics.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or independent external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, or superiority to Linux.
